grid_resolution_topology.interpretation: The frozen threshold/best-partner C -> I -> S median winner sequence is not an artefact of the 21-point (0.05-spaced) starting-state grid.

smooth_weighted_feedback.interpretation: Removing both the hard service threshold and the best-partner switch preserves a C/I boundary crossing in every seed, but does not reproduce the large-k starting-state takeover. The robust mechanistic claim is transient C-to-I rank reversal under nonlinear feedback, not a universal C-to-I-to-S three-regime sequence.

fixed_state_negative_control.interpretation: Without plant-state movement, interaction nonadditivity can still overtake community variance, but starting-state dominance does not emerge.

absolute_ss_scaling.interpretation: The normalized crossover is not only denominator arithmetic. Under the frozen rule, C contracts much faster than I while S is approximately flat over the audited finite range; under smooth feedback C again contracts faster than I, allowing transient I dominance.

paper_facing_boundary: Grid resolution concern is closed for 21/41/81 points.
C-to-I rank reversal is robust to removal of the hard threshold and best-partner switch across all six frozen seeds.
The later S-dominant regime is not update-rule invariant and must not be presented as a general nonlinear-averaging law.
Synthetic k remains uncalibrated to any natural richness/diversity coordinate.
